messages:
Eli: thanks for today, leaving an open thread for any strategy follow-ups — ask short Qs here.
Maya: quick framing: mission unchanged: predictable, production-ready inference across hosted/dedicated/private. our edge is serving reliability and cost predictability.
Lena: quick one for GTM: should external messaging lead with 'predictability' or 'unit economics'? which converts better?
Jordan: depends on buyer. platform engineers = predictability/observability. CFOs/ops = unit economics. craft two one-liners.
Harper: competitor Q: hypers bundle model+infra. do we integrate with them or call them out directly in sales?
Maya: pragmatic: integrate where customers want (marketplace listings), but call out scenarios we uniquely solve: private installs, precise SLAs, rollback tooling, and token-level cost visibility.
Diego: ops ask: Dedicated SLA timeline — procurement needs a quarter.
Jordan: target initial 99.9% SLA in the next fiscal quarter; runbooks and failover docs will land with it.
Tess: product: will Optimize ever auto-apply quantization changes?
Maya: roadmap: suggestions + diagnostics now; opt-in safe auto-apply later after more validation.
Lena: marketing ask: can we get a short reproducible benchmark to cite externally?
Eli: yes — eng + marketing will produce a reproducible benchmark repo and a 2-slide summary with configs and key numbers.
Harper: messaging nuance: how do we say 'we're serving-first' without sounding model-agnostic?
Jordan: phrase it as 'we maximize the value of your chosen model in production' and include eval+rollback examples.
AllHandsBot: poll: "Which lead message should we push next week?" options: 1) Predictability & SLAs 2) Unit economics 3) Private + compliance 4) Observability. React 1/2/3/4.
Eli: action items: PMs to draft two hero messages, eng+marketing to scope benchmark, solutions to draft Dedicated onboarding/runbook checklist. we'll synthesize an FAQ + slide pack by end of week. keep short threads here. :rocket:
